intro_messages.speaker: Mari
intro_messages.message: Not bad at all for a first fight. Now let’s get you to Westin — we’re not far now.
intro_messages.message_fr: Pas mal du tout pour un premier combat. Direction Westin, maintenant — on n’est plus très loin.

intro_messages.speaker: Urza Mathin
intro_messages.message: Oh, what’s this? A lady and her loyal squire travelin’ south on this dangerous road? Tell ya what, we can offer ya protection ’round here for a small fee.
intro_messages.message_fr: Mais qu'vons nous là ? Une gente dame et son fidèle écuyer, voyageant au Sud sur s'te dangereuse route ? Vas-y voir, nous p'vons sûrement vous offrir notre protection. Contre z'une honnête rémunération, bien entendu.

intro_messages.speaker: Deoran
intro_messages.message: Do you take us for fools? I ride south to reinforce Westin’s venerable South Guard, on orders from the King to ensure the region is kept safe and secure!
intro_messages.message_fr: Vous nous prenez pour des lapins de six semaines ? Je chevauche vers le Sud pour renforcer la vénérable Garde du Sud de Westin, selon la volonté du roi d'assurer la sécurité dans cette région !

intro_messages.speaker: Deoran
intro_messages.message: The only danger around here is you, and I intend to put an end to it. Men, raise your spears!
intro_messages.message_fr: Le seul danger ici c'est vous, et j'ai bien l'intention d'y mettre un terme. Arrière, vils marauds ! Soldats, à vos lances !

intro_messages.speaker: Urza Mathin
intro_messages.message: Hah, like it would be that easy, child. I’m Urza Mathin, eldest of the four Urza brothers, and these are my thugs. Time to show you who the real power is in these parts!
intro_messages.message_fr: Ha Ha, c'n'est pas aussi simple que ça, gamin. J'suis Urza Mathin, aîné des quatre frères Urza, et voici mes hommes de main. L'est temps d'vous montrer qui c'est le plus fort dans cette région !

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Suit yourself. I’m sure you won’t need my help against those bandits anyway.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: (Bows) A pleasure to make your acquaintance, Captain.

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: Wondering about those percentages that appear on the ground when you move a unit? That’s your soldiers’ terrain defense — their chance to evade enemy attacks.

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Amazing, you know how to ride your horse. Now let’s see if you know how to swing your sword.

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Behold!

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: ...a quintain? You want me to attack a practice dummy?

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: You have fifty pounds of armor and a horse, rookie. I’m fairly sure you’ll win.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: Hey, this quintain fights back! I’m not about to lose to a dummy — let me attack again!

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Nice try, but you already used up your chance to attack. Now it’s the quintain’s turn to act.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: The dummy gets a turn?

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Why not? It’s a magical quintain, on loan from the wizards’ academy at Alduin. It strikes twice per attack, and will sting something fierce if it hits you. Brace yourself!

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: To end your turn, open the menu (MENU button) and choose “End Turn”.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: I’m injured; this is more dangerous than I expected. I should retreat to a village, where I can catch my breath and bandage my wounds.

a.reason:
Move to a village first!
(press “u” if you need to undo a move)

a.speaker: narrator
a.caption: Undo
a.message: Tip: Press the D button if you ever want to undo a move. Attacks cannot be undone.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: I’m already seriously injured! If I attack now, I am sure to be vanquished. By a dummy, no less.

a.description: End your turn on a village

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: You’ve captured a village, which now flies the red-and-white colors of our banner. Each village we own provides us with some income — and importantly for you, provides a place to rest and recover.

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: Starting your turn in a village will heal you for 8 hitpoints. End your turn now.

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Congratulations, you ran away from the dummy and licked your wounds in a village. I hope you’re proud.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: I’ve had enough of being humiliated by this dummy. Time to recruit some proper soldiers and smash that thing to pieces.

a.speaker: narrator
a.message:
The golden crown above Deoran’s HP bar indicates that he’s a leader: he can recruit new units when standing on a castle’s keep hex.

In most scenarios, you will lose if your leader is killed. Use Deoran enough to build his experience, but not so aggressively that he’s at risk of dying!

a.speaker: narrator
a.caption: Undo
a.message: Tip: Press the D button if you ever want to undo a move. Attacks cannot be undone.

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: Move onto your keep, then open the menu (MENU button) and choose “Recruit” to recruit new soldiers.

a.speaker: narrator
a.caption: Undo
a.message: Tip: Press the D button if you ever want to undo a move. Attacks cannot be undone.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: At your service, Commander Deoran! You should still have some gold left — I suggest you keep recruiting more soldiers.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: The quintain is repairing itself! Come on men, let’s go finish it off!

a.speaker: narrator
a.message:
In addition to the +8 healing provided by a village, units will also regenerate 2 hitpoints if they spend their turn resting: neither moving nor fighting.

This “rest-healing” stacks with village healing.

a.speaker: narrator
a.caption: Undo
a.message: Tip: Press the D button if you ever want to undo a move. Attacks cannot be undone.

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: ...he’s fine. Just out cold, and of no use to you for the rest of our journey.

a.speaker: second_unit
a.message: Hooray! The dummy is destroyed, and I’ve gained valuable combat experience!

a.speaker: narrator
a.message:
Units gain a small amount of experience when attacking or defending, but gain much more by striking a finishing blow, especially against high-level enemies.

With enough experience, a soldier will advance to a powerful level 2 unit.

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Not bad, you’ve smashed it to splinters. ...is it too late to mention that I was supposed to return that after we finished training? Maybe I can find a replacement once we reach Westin.

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Of course before we can reach Westin, we’ll first have to fight our way past these bandits.

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Are you... actually trying to fight the quintain? We don’t have all day. Hurry up and beat it.

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: We’re going to have to cut things short, rookie. Look: bandits on the south road!

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Get a move on, rookie! I’m sure those bandits have called for reinforcements — you’re running out of time to finish them off.

a.speaker: Urza Mathin
a.message: Reinforcements from my brothers! Excellent. These lands belong to the brothers Urza!

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: We’ve run out of time, and now more enemies have arrived! We’ll have to retreat and bring more soldiers some other time. I really thought Deoran could handle this on his own...

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: You are beaten, you bloodthirsty, balding bandit! Accosting travelers between Weldyn and Westin; what is the meaning of this? How have you become so bold as to strike at even trained soldiers!?

a.speaker: Urza Mathin
a.message: How... impossible... no! If I die... so will you!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I have failed my kingdom and duty...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Yeah... I should’ve figured I wouldn’t get a happy ending...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I have given all in service of my kingdom...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: May the Light guide you where I have failed...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I have lost everything helping the humans... Now they will surely perish!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I perish! Such wasted potential! I’d gained much experience, and was close to becoming something more...

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: One of your high-experience units has died! Take care to protect your experienced soldiers, so that they can eventually advance to powerful Level 2 veterans.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Argh, I fall! All my hard-won battle experience is lost! I will not be easy to replace, Deoran...

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: One of your high-level veterans has died! Take care to protect your promoted soldiers, so that you can recall them in future battles.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: What the—

a.speaker: Zombie Mathin
a.message: Gruhh...

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Look out!

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Undead again. As if losing one arm to these things wasn’t bad enough, now they’re back for my second.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: I’ve never seen the like before in my life! That man clearly died, then stood right back up again! You say you’ve fought these things before, Mari?

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Yeah, I have. And no, simple bandits aren’t supposed to know how to create them. This reeks of black magic; powerful black magic.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: This brother said he was the eldest of four — the other three are doubtless still alive and causing trouble. How did petty outlaws get their hands on magic like this?

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Maybe the locals in town will know something. Come on, let’s hurry onwards towards Westin, and hope we don’t run into any more trouble on the way.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: They’ve broken through the trapdoor and entered the refugee cellar! Even if we could still manage to win by force of arms, Westin is doomed without its people...

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: Taste cold steel!

a.speaker: narrator
a.message:
One of your units has reached max XP, and has advanced a level! It is now significantly more powerful, and has been fully healed!

Every unit’s full description is shown in the info panel at the bottom of the screen.
My healing magic is potent, but I cannot use it to heal myself. I’ll have to spend some time in a village to recover.

a.speaker: Urza Mathin
a.message: The sun begins to set! Soon these Wesnoth soldiers will falter in the dark, while my thugs and I will fight at our best. Press the attack!

a.speaker: Mari
a.message:
Careful, Deoran. Unless you have overwhelming numbers, you may want to hunker down and hold a defensive position until dawn. Castles and especially villages (because they heal) make for good defensive positions.

 Capturing villages will also increase your income, which you can use to recruit more soldiers.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: Day has come! We will be strongest in the light — now is the time for us to attack and drive these bandits from our lands. To me, men of the South Guard!

a.speaker: Urza Mathin
a.message: Ha, this will be an easy victory! These soldiers’ young commander must be a fool, for he fights my thugs at night while I am strong and he is weak.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I just made a ranged attack! I had to stand right next to this Quintain (yes, this is different from how most games handle ranged attacks), but because the dummy has no ranged weapon of its own it was unable to retaliate.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I just made a ranged attack! I had to stand right next to this $second_unit.language_name (yes, this is different from how most games handle ranged attacks), but because the $second_unit.language_name has no ranged weapon of its own it was unable to retaliate.

a.message: I just made a ranged attack! I had to stand right next to this $second_unit.language_name (yes, this is different from how most games handle ranged attacks), but because the $second_unit.language_name has no ranged weapon of his own he was unable to retaliate.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I missed all $consecutive_misses strikes! I tried my best, but this enemy had a high chance to evade. I might have had better odds attacking a different enemy.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: A good commander understands the odds, and knows how to both exploit good luck and mitigate bad luck. After all, both good and bad luck are equally likely!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I got lucky and hit all $consecutive_hits strikes! Good luck will sometimes happen, but a good commander knows how to win without relying on it. After all, bad luck happens just as often as good luck!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I missed all $consecutive_misses strikes, even though my enemy had a low chance to evade! That’s unlucky, but bad luck happens just as often as good luck — a good commander knows how to plan around both!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I hit all $consecutive_hits strikes, even though my enemy had a high chance to evade! Luck works both ways — sometimes I miss strikes when I was likely to hit, but sometimes I also hit strikes that I was likely to miss — like now!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Our bows and spears are nearly useless against these skeletons! They have nothing for our shafts to pierce but air!

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: Every unit’s damage resistances and vulnerabilities are shown in the info panel at the bottom of the screen.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: Are you going to help fight? We must drive these villains from the road!

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Officially, I’m only here as an observer. These ruffians don’t look too dangerous — you and your professional soldiers should be able to make short work of them, even without my sword.

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Besides, it only took $quintain_killers.length of you to deal with my dummy. What’s a dozen muscly bandits compared to that?

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Oh, now you want my help? I thought you were too clever to listen to my tutorial.

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: Get out of my face!

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: What happened to being a passive observer?

a.speaker: Mari
a.message: ...self-defense doesn’t count.
Stop right there! Not one hair further or I’ll bash your head in!
